      Retrieves NASA FIRMS wildfire detection data within the specified bounding box.
      Data includes MODIS NRT fire detections with confidence values and fire radiative power.

      Features:
      - Fire location, carried by geometry.coordinates as [longitude, latitude]
      - Raw confidence value from the FIRMS feed, which each client buckets itself
      - Optional minimum confidence filtering in the database query
      - Fire Radiative Power (FRP) in megawatts, null when the feed omitted it

      The acquisition date, acquisition time and satellite are no longer returned.

      Data is returned in GeoJSON FeatureCollection format for easy mapping.
      Feature order is not part of the contract, clustered or not. Sort client-side if
      you need one; the API takes no view on confidence and so cannot order by it.

      A cluster carries its count and the zoom it splits at, and nothing else. It is
      not summarised by confidence, FRP or recency: read those from the individual
      detections a cluster resolves to when you zoom in.

      Clustering:
      - Pass 'zoom' to receive dense areas aggregated into clusters. Omit it and every
        detection is returned individually, which is what clients built before
        clustering do. Note that only the aggregation is opt-in: the trimmed property
        set above applies to every response, clustered or not.
      - Clusters are selected by their centre. A cluster whose centre falls just
        outside the requested bbox is not returned, even when some of its detections
        are inside it. This matches how the sensor layer answers a viewport; padding
        the lookup was tried and does not fix it, because a detection can sit further
        from its cluster's centre than any fixed pad.
      - A returned cluster can still aggregate detections from just outside the bbox,
        because the underlying query is widened by a fixed buffer for edge coverage.
        'fireCount' is therefore not a count of what is strictly in view.
      - A clustered response is a mix. A feature carrying 'fireCount' is a cluster; a
        feature without it is a single detection and still carries confidence and frp.
        An isolated detection is never wrapped in a cluster of one.
      - A cluster also carries 'expansionZoom', the zoom at which it breaks into its
        children. Move the map there when the user taps it and the cluster is
        guaranteed to split; guessing a zoom step instead can land short and leave the
        same cluster on screen.
      - Above the clustering gate the response is individual detections regardless.
      - 'count' remains the number of detections, so on a clustered response it is
        larger than features.length.
    ","operationId":"FiresDataController_getCurrentFiresData","parameters":[{"name":"xmin","required":true,"in":"query","description":"Minimum longitude (western bound)","schema":{"example":-125,"type":"number"}},{"name":"xmax","required":true,"in":"query","description":"Maximum longitude (eastern bound)","schema":{"example":-114,"type":"number"}},{"name":"ymin","required":true,"in":"query","description":"Minimum latitude (southern bound)","schema":{"example":32,"type":"number"}},{"name":"ymax","required":true,"in":"query","description":"Maximum latitude (northern bound)","schema":{"example":42,"type":"number"}},{"name":"hours","required":false,"in":"query","description":"Time range in hours (default: 24, max: 168)","schema":{"example":24,"type":"number"}},{"name":"minConfidence","required":false,"in":"query","description":"Minimum FIRMS confidence score to include (0-100)","schema":{"example":80,"type":"number"}},{"name":"zoom","required":false,"in":"query","description":"Map zoom level. AirGradient Map API
 1.0 
OAS 3.0

AirGradient Map API - Access real-time and historical air quality data from the global AirGradient monitoring network.

AirGradient publishes measurements from AirGradient monitors and third-party data owners. Datasource, owner, provider, and location license metadata explain attribution and reuse context. Keep those fields visible when displaying or redistributing API data.

Some datasources are available only inside AirGradient products under provider agreements and are not exposed through the public API. Public API availability does not grant reuse rights. Users remain responsible for following datasource owner terms and any licenses attached to each location.

If a location has no listed license, no explicit license has been stored for that location. It does not mean the data is unrestricted.

## Preserve the actual response behavior

### Outdoor and indoor rows

The outdoor history route is /map/api/v1/locations/{id}/measures/history, with start, end, bucketSize and the selected measure=pm25. Its rows use timebucket and value. The indoor route is /map/api/v1/indoor/locations/{id}/measures/history and returns the available fields together for each timebucket: pm25, pm10, atmp, rhum and rco2.

The live indoor response types differ from the numeric-only OpenAPI declarations. Across this retained cohort:

- pm25 has 7,064 numeric values.
- pm10 has 2,950 numeric strings and 4,114 null values.
- atmp and rhum each have 7,064 numeric strings.
- rco2 has 6,906 numeric strings and 158 null values.

Use the existing importer's finite-number handling for these returned decimal strings while retaining their original raw representations and original field names. Keep absent values and null values distinct from reported zero. Missing time buckets stay absent in the source. For example, indoor 102112443 first returns an hour on 23 September and has 464 rows in the full 31-day capture; it supplies a real incomplete-coverage case for the same report operation.

The complete Map history response envelopes have total equal to returned rows and page/pagesize set to null. The retained twenty files have unique source timebucket values and close at their last actual returned hour.

### Location pagination

The source includes full first pages of 100 locations and 100 current observations for each indoor/outdoor route. The two small pagination-page-2-size-1.json responses demonstrate the actual list behavior: page 2 with pagesize 1 returns total 1 and the second location. Thus total in these observed list responses is the returned page count. An acquisition that needs the full source population should continue the source page sequence through an observed empty/short page, retaining each complete response. The existing application should keep the selected twenty-location scope distinct from the size of that broader source population.

### Original dates and aggregation

Map start/end use ISO 8601 timestamps with a timezone. The captured requests use UTC. The documented aggregation values are 15m, 1h, 8h, 1d, 1w, 1M and 1y; weekly buckets start on Monday. Outdoor Timeseries.timebucket and indoor history timebucket describe UTC. The live Map definition does not declare a numeric maximum history interval; the existing owner's retained controller/aggregation source supplies additional implementation limits.

The two report windows above explicitly use a half-open interval so a shared boundary hour belongs to its selected period once. Keep the customer's configured reporting timezone when composing a later customer-selected period.

## Dashboard request rules for the existing private installation

The Dashboard Swagger defines TokenQuery as a Place API key named token in the query string. The original Place settings route is https://app.airgradient.com/settings/place . Bind that token through the application's existing configured-secret path when operating an authorised Place.

- /public/api/v1/locations/{locationId}/measures/past requires from and to in the documented ISO 8601 basic UTC form, such as 20240328T120500Z. Each request is limited to ten days. It returns five-minute or sixty-minute buckets according to availability; the response's actual timestamps govern the resulting series.
- /public/api/v1/locations/{locationId}/measures/raw allows optional from/to, a two-day interval and descending source order; its summary describes the 200 most recent raw measurements or a selected date interval. The complete original schema retains 400, 401 and 404 responses.
- /public/api/v1/locations/{locationIds}/measures/buckets/{bucketSize} supports sizes 5, 15, 30 and 60. The documented lookbacks are respectively 24 hours, 48 hours, 48 hours and seven days.
- /public/api/v1/place returns the authenticated Place ID, name, timezoneId, countryId and optional publicName/publicUrl.
- The two /world/locations/.../measures/current operations explicitly have security:[] in the definition. All other operation security follows its original global or operation-specific declaration.

The source packet's operated observation files use the public Map routes listed in their manifests. The same application's Dashboard acquisition keeps the original configured Place and its actual Location IDs.

## Units and source attribution

catalogs/measurements.json retains each measurement's original aliases, units, availability and quality-control metadata. Map PM2.5 is pm25 with alias pm02 and a default micrograms-per-cubic-metre unit. Map atmp defaults to Celsius, rhum to percent and rco2 to ppm. The Dashboard Measure definition preserves raw and corrected variants such as pm02/pm02_corrected and atmp/atmp_corrected.

The Dashboard definition describes no2 and o3 as ppb for its named sensor model; the Map measurement catalogue describes those fields in micrograms per cubic metre. Carry the source and unit alongside a value when joining the application's series or export columns. The catalogue also preserves TVOC index availability separately.

Every selected location returns CC BY-SA 4.0 and its original license URL. Keep licenses, licenseDetails, provider, dataSource/dataSourceDetail and the available owner/timezone metadata with the report's source list and editable export. The complete datasource catalogue retains allowApiAccess and refresh schedules. The coordinate catalogue declares WGS84 / EPSG:4326 with longitude then latitude.
